brief: Russell 2000 broke its longer-term trend line and sits well below its 200-day moving average, with technical damage, credit stress, and systematic selling compounding the decline. Deteriorating high-yield credit, tied to CoreWeave-related contagion, pushed CDX 5-year high-yield spreads to six-month highs. Goldman's High Yield Debt Sensitive basket plunged 4.9%, and Russell, given its sub-investment-grade exposure, fell 1.9%. Since July, CFTC data shows hedge fund Russell short positioning rising alongside widening CDX spreads, so short positioning is now very large. CTAs have also sold aggressively and are now their shortest Russell position since 2023. The note argues this chain, deteriorating credit driving record shorts from both hedge funds and CTAs, sets up a potential squeeze: large short positioning raises the odds of a sharp short-covering rally, and CTAs' extreme short stance leaves room for systematic buying if Russell turns higher. It also cites supporting factors: Russell has tracked the 10-year yield closely and the relationship is diverging, the index is deeply oversold, and the last time it undershot its 200-day average buyers stepped in and reversed it sharply. The note frames this as a possible third crowded-trade blowup after AI and bonds but does not call the reversal outright.
